title: The policy file evidence.yml
description: Says what evidence each kind of change must show (spec section 8.1). Every key is optional, so an empty file is a valid policy. A key with nothing under it, such as kinds:, is the same as no key. Exhibit refuses to run on a file that does not pass this schema.

version.description: The format of the file. This Exhibit reads format 3 only. null, from version: with nothing after it, is the same as no version.

test_command.description: The command that runs the tests on the base and on the head (spec 9.3).

test_results.description: The JUnit XML file that the test command writes.

test_timeout_seconds.description: The time limit for one run of the test command (spec 9.3), at most 86400 (one day). A run that takes longer is stopped, with every process it started, and the requirement is error. Absent means 1800.

fix_signals.description: The signals that mark a PR as a fix (spec 9.1). null or absent means the defaults [label:bug, title:fix, branch:fix/].

source_paths.description: Globs on file paths that mark source code (spec 9.1). A PR that adds a file that one of them matches is a feature. null or absent means no path is source, so only the feature label marks a feature.

site.description: The Jira site, such as https://acme.atlassian.net (spec 9.1).

issue_types.description: The issue types that count as a bug. Absent means [Bug]. A list replaces the default.

found_field.description: The Jira field that says where a bug was found, such as customfield_10042. Needs escaped_values.

escaped_values.description: The values of found_field that mean the bug got out to users, such as [Production]. Needs found_field.

jira.description: The Jira site and fields for the tracker:jira fix signal (spec 9.1). The token comes from the env variable JIRA_API_TOKEN, never from this file.

mutation_budget_seconds.description: The time budget for one mutation run, in seconds (spec 9.5). Absent means 600.

mutation_setup.description: The command that installs what the tests need in the head worktree before Stryker or mutmut runs, such as npm ci (spec 9.5).

mutation_python.description: The command that starts the Python of a changed Python file's project, with the project's packages and mutmut 3.8.1, such as uv run --with mutmut==3.8.1 python (spec 9.5). It runs with sh in the project's folder. Absent means python3.

mutation_test_files.description: Globs of the test files that Stryker runs, such as ["test/**/*.test.js"] (spec 9.5). Each one runs as node FILE.

probe_timeout_seconds.description: The time limit for each probe (spec 9.6), at most 86400 (one day). A probe that runs longer is stopped and fails. Absent means 600.

storage.description: Where exhibit publish stores an exhibit (spec 9.12). data-branch commits it to the data branch. local writes it to a folder. Absent means data-branch.

data_branch.description: The name of the data branch (spec 9.12). Absent means exhibit-data.

local_path.description: The folder that storage: local writes to, relative to the repo (spec 9.12). Absent means .exhibit/out.

kinds.description: Each key names a kind of change, such as relay-core.

match.description: Globs on the changed file paths.

items.description: One evidence item. A bare name is tests-before-after or failing-before. An item with fields is a mapping with one key, the item type.

tests-before-after.description: The tests ran on the base and on the head, and pass on the head (spec 9.3).

failing-before.description: A test the PR added or changed fails on the base and passes on the head (spec 9.4).

when.description: Limits the item to PRs classified as fix or feature.

mutation.description: The catch rate on the changed lines is at least min (spec 9.5).

probe.description: A named command exits 0 on the head and writes its artifacts (spec 9.6).

author.description: hidden: the builder cannot see the check (spec 9.7).

source.description: The defect IDs the rule came from (spec 9.9).

default.description: The rules for a PR that matches no kind.

tests-before-after.description: The tests ran on the base and on the head, and pass on the head (spec 9.3).

failing-before.description: A test the PR added or changed fails on the base and passes on the head (spec 9.4).

mutation.description: The catch rate on the changed lines is at least min (spec 9.5).

probe.description: A named command exits 0 on the head and writes its artifacts (spec 9.6).

author.description: hidden: the builder cannot see the check (spec 9.7).

equivalent_mutants.description: Surviving mutants that a person marked as equivalent: a change that cannot alter what the code does (spec 9.5). A mutant that survived, or that no test reached, and that matches a mark in all five of file, line_text, mutator, original and replacement, does not count in the catch rate. exhibit check reads the marks from the base commit, as it reads the rest of this file, so a change to them needs a person. Copy each of the five values as the quoted JSON string that evidence.json gives, so YAML reads it as the same text.

file.description: The path of the mutated file in the repo, as evidence.json gives it.

line_text.description: The text of the line the mutant starts on, as evidence.json gives it: trimmed, with each run of white space as one space. It is in the key in place of the line number, so a mark still holds when lines above it move.

mutator.description: The mutator that made the mutant, such as EqualityOperator.

original.description: The code that the mutant replaced, as evidence.json gives it. Copy it as the quoted JSON string from evidence.json, such as "\"\"", because YAML reads some code without quotes as another type: true as a boolean, [] as a list, and "" as empty text.

replacement.description: The code the mutant put in its place, as evidence.json gives it. Copy it as the quoted JSON string from evidence.json, such as "\"\"", because YAML reads some code without quotes as another type: true as a boolean, [] as a list, and "" as empty text.

reason.description: Why the mutant cannot change what the code does, in words a reviewer can check.
